title: Move split_line off strtok
summary: Swap the shared state of strtok for strtok_r, then stop chewing up the caller's line.

turns.user: split_line mixes up results when two threads hit it. also blows up on long lines

assistant.body: strtok keeps its next position in static storage inside the function, so two threads walk over each other's state. Three things to fix: move to strtok_r so the position lives in the caller, take fields as an argument instead of sharing one static array, and bound the count, because today anything past 8 fields writes off the end. This also leaves the caller's line untouched.

turns.user: you said it leaves line alone but the debugger shows the commas turned into zeros. we use line again after this

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect on that point. strtok_r only fixes reentrancy. It still overwrites each delimiter with a NUL exactly like strtok does. Taking line as const and copying it into a caller supplied scratch buffer, then cutting up the copy. The length is checked before the copy, and a line that does not fit returns -1.

turns.user: we started getting tab separated files too. add tab to the delimiters. and that comment at the top is wrong now

assistant.body: Right, the comment no longer matches. Adding the tab to DELIM and rewriting the comment in the same pass. Worth knowing: strtok_r folds a run of delimiters into one, so an empty field between two commas disappears. If those have to survive, strsep is the right tool instead.
sed -i '' -e 's/#define DELIM ","/#define DELIM ",\\t"/' -e 's|/\* split a comma separated line \*/|/* split a line on commas or tabs */|' src/csv/parse.c
